home.metaTitle: My journey as a blind developer | Martin Jurk
home.metaDescription: Rehabilitation at QuikStep, apprenticeship at the DKFZ, work in cancer research – with searchable practical tips on screen readers, the Linux and Windows terminal, SQL, Rust and Kubernetes.
home.title: From rehabilitation to cancer research
home.lead: I lost my sight in 2015 and started again in software development. Here I show the three most important parts of that journey – each with practical tips on how I work in the terminal with a screen reader.
home.fact4: practical tips for Windows, Linux and macOS
home.chaptersIntro: Each chapter tells one part of the story and has expandable tip cards with copyable commands and interactive demos.
home.searchIntro: Search for tools, commands or topics – for example “psql”, “Fenrir” or “PowerShell”.
home.howText: For employers who want to see how I work. For people who program with a screen reader or want to learn it. And for anyone with a blind colleague or apprentice on their team.
home.contactText: I am open to backend and DevOps roles – remote, or within commuting distance of Karlsruhe. I am also happy to answer questions about these tips or your own setup.

sql.title: Demo: what a screen reader makes of SQL output
sql.intro: The same query, two output formats. Switch the format and compare what gets read out.
sql.speech: What it sounds like with a screen reader
sql.speechTable: Plus dash dash dash dash plus dash dash dash dash dash dash dash dash dash dash plus … vertical bar id vertical bar company vertical bar status vertical bar … plus dash dash dash …
sql.speechLine: id equals 1. company equals Example Ltd. status equals open. Blank. id equals 2. company equals Sample Inc. status equals interview.

form.title: Demo: error messages that get through – or don’t
form.intro: Submit the form with an invalid email address. Compare what a screen reader announces in both versions.
form.error: Please enter a valid email address.
form.success: Thank you, the address is valid.
form.announce: What the screen reader says in the field
form.announceGoodText: Email, edit text, invalid entry, {{value}}. Please enter a valid email address.
form.explainBad: The error message is visible below the field but not linked to it. Focus stays on the button and nobody announces the error.
form.explainGood: aria-invalid and aria-describedby link field and message, focus moves into the field, and a live region announces the error immediately.
